title: What's it like?
goal: Describe people, things, and places: adjectives that change form, where they go after the noun, and how to compare.
bekal: make adjectives agree in gender and number
put adjectives in the right place

dialogs.title: Dialogo — Com'è il tuo nuovo appartamento?
dialogs.intro: Budi has just moved. Giulia wants all the details.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.id: So, what's the new apartment like?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Piccolo ma luminoso. Ha due finestre grandi.
lines.id: Small but bright. It has two big windows.
lines.literal: small but bright. has two windows big.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: No, in periferia. È più tranquillo e meno caro.
lines.id: No, on the outskirts. It's quieter and cheaper.
lines.literal: no, in outskirts. is more quiet and less expensive.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.id: And the neighbors? Are they nice?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: La signora del piano di sotto è molto gentile. Un po' curiosa, però.
lines.id: The lady downstairs is very kind. A bit nosy, though.
lines.literal: the lady of-the floor of below is very kind. a bit curious, though.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Sa già il mio nome, il mio lavoro e il nome del mio gatto.
lines.id: She already knows my name, my job, and my cat's name.
lines.literal: knows already the my name, the my job and the name of-the my cat.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Classica signora italiana! E il tuo gatto sta bene lì?
lines.id: A classic Italian lady! And is your cat happy there?
lines.literal: classic lady italian! and the your cat stays well there?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Benissimo. Dorme tutto il giorno sul davanzale.
lines.id: Very happy. He sleeps all day on the windowsill.
lines.literal: very-well. sleeps all the day on-the windowsill.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: È più fortunato di noi, allora.
lines.literal: is more lucky than us, then.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Molto più fortunato. E non paga l'affitto.
lines.id: Much luckier. And he doesn't pay rent.
lines.literal: much more lucky. and not pays the rent.

notes: **Adjectives come after the noun.** *Un appartamento piccolo*, *una finestra grande*. This is the reverse of English, so it takes a little getting used to.

**But a small group goes in front.** *Bello*, *brutto*, *buono*, *cattivo*, *grande*, *piccolo*, *nuovo*, *vecchio*, *giovane*, *lungo* often come first, especially when the quality is seen as natural to the thing: *il nuovo appartamento*, *una bella giornata*.

**Position can change the meaning.** *Un amico vecchio* = a friend who is old. *Un vecchio amico* = an old (long-time) friend. *Una macchina nuova* = a brand-new car; *una nuova macchina* = a car that's new to me. You don't need to master this now — just know it exists.
**The adjective follows the noun, not the speaker.** When Budi says *la casa è piccola*, it's feminine because *casa* is feminine — not because of who is talking.

**Molto has two faces.** Before an adjective it means "very" and **never changes**: *molto gentile*, *molto gentili*. Before a noun it means "many/much" and **does change**: *molti amici*, *molte cose*.
**Benissimo, bellissimo, carissimo.** The ending *-issimo* means "extremely" and fits on almost any adjective. Italians use it constantly: *buonissimo*, *facilissimo*, *stanchissimo*.
**Simpatico isn't "sympathetic".** It means nice, fun, easy to get along with. Its opposite is *antipatico*. It's one of the most common adjectives for judging people.
**Però means "but", just like ma**, but it can also sit at the end of a sentence — like English "though": *Un po' curiosa, però*.

grammars.title: Two groups of adjectives
body: Italian adjectives fall into two groups by their ending. The first has four forms, the second only two.
after: The second group is much easier: one form for singular, one for plural, regardless of gender. It has many common members: *grande*, *gentile*, *interessante*, *difficile*, *facile*, *giovane*, *veloce*, *triste*.
A mixed group of men and women takes the masculine plural: *Marco e Giulia sono simpatici*.
Nationality adjectives follow the same rules: *italiano/italiana/italiani/italiane*, but *francese/francesi* because it ends in -e.

grammars.title: Comparing
body: Three patterns cover all the comparisons you need at A1.

head: Meaning
Pattern
Example
rows: Roma è più grande di Bologna.
Bologna è meno cara di Milano.
È la città più bella d'Italia.

after: Four adjectives have their own comparative forms and don't use *più*: *buono → migliore* (better), *cattivo → peggiore* (worse), *grande → maggiore* (bigger/older), *piccolo → minore* (smaller/younger).
*Di* merges with the article as usual: *più caro del pane*, *più bella della piazza*.

blocks.text: *Caro* carries two meanings at once: "expensive" and "dear". An Italian letter opens with *Caro Marco*, and that's clearly not a comment on price.

blocks.title: Describing people
items: Hair: *Ha i capelli neri / biondi / castani / corti / lunghi / ricci* (curly) / *lisci* (straight).
Eyes: *Ha gli occhi neri / azzurri / verdi / marroni.*
Personality: *È simpatico, gentile, timido, allegro, serio.*
Asking: *Com'è?* (what is he/she like) — don't mix it up with *Come sta?* (how is he/she doing).
Rough age: *È giovane.* / *È anziano.* / *Ha una trentina d'anni.* (about thirty-something)

blocks.text: Notice that hair and eyes use *avere* and the plural: *ha i capelli neri*, literally "he has black hairs". Italian counts hair as many strands, not one mass.

exercises.prompt: Make the adjective in brackets agree.
Compare the two using più… di. The first one named is the "more" one.

items: The apartment is small but bright.
He has black hair and brown eyes.
It's the most beautiful city in Italy.

exercises.prompt: Fill in molto, molti, molte, or molta.

answers: piccola — simpatici — grandi — stanco — alte — interessante
Roma è più grande di Bologna. — Milano è più cara di Napoli. — Il treno è più veloce dell'autobus. — Il giapponese è più difficile dell'italiano. — La periferia è più tranquilla del centro.
L'appartamento è piccolo ma luminoso. — Il mio vicino è molto gentile. — È più alto di me. — Ha i capelli neri e gli occhi marroni. — È la città più bella d'Italia. — Sono stanchissimo.
